subtopic: CUDA / Stream, Event, and asynchronous ordering
learningObjective: Understand CUDA stream ordering semantics and how events synchronize across streams.
stem: Which statements about CUDA streams and events are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: All non-default streams block each other by default; concurrent execution across streams requires an explicit `cudaSetStreamPriority(concurrent=true)` call before use.
`cudaEventRecord` is a synchronous host operation that returns only after the event has been observed by the device; it blocks the calling CPU thread.
Kernels launched on the same non-default stream execute in program order; kernels on different streams may execute concurrently subject to resource availability.

`cudaEventRecord(e, s1)` followed by `cudaStreamWaitEvent(s2, e, 0)` makes any subsequent work on `s2` wait until the event fires (i.e., until all work enqueued on `s1` before the record has completed), enabling cross-stream dependencies without blocking the host thread.

explanation: A: Within one stream, work is serialized in issue order; different streams can overlap (subject to compute/copy engine availability). B: Events provide a cross-stream synchronization primitive: record an event on stream A, tell stream B to wait, and B's subsequent work is ordered after A's pre-record work. Neither operation blocks the host. C is wrong: non-default streams are concurrent by default; no priority flag is required. D is wrong: `cudaEventRecord` is asynchronous — it enqueues the record; use `cudaEventSynchronize` if you want the host to wait.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: streams are concurrent by default.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: intra-stream ordered, inter-stream may overlap.

assumptions: Standard CUDA runtime semantics as documented.
Default stream = 0 behavior is per-thread or legacy depending on compile flag; question focuses on non-default streams.
nonImplications: Does not imply that any two streams always overlap; hardware resources (copy engines, SM count) still constrain concurrency.
Does not imply `cudaStreamWaitEvent` blocks the host.

distractorRationales.A: Wrong claim about default stream blocking.
